$comment: Every sound in the game is SYNTHESISED at load from these numbers (T-6.16). No audio file is loaded, shipped, or referenced by the build. That is a deliberate match for the greybox art: the visuals are untextured primitives, so the audio is untextured waveforms, and the two read as one intentional style rather than as placeholder. It also keeps the build tiny and the whole mix tunable without a recompile. Colours of noise and exact frequencies were chosen by ear against the arena, not derived. NOTE: the repo root still carries an `Audio/` folder of sourced .mp3 files from an earlier direction. Nothing reads them — keep them as reference or delete them, but they are not part of the game.
$busNote: T-6.20. Every clip names a bus; the played volume is master * bus * the clip's own gain. Buses are the mix, clip gain is the balance within a bus. `crowd` sits low on purpose — it is texture under the fight, and the moment it competes with an impact it is wrong.
$clipNote: kind: saw (buzzy periodic, for motors and blades), noise (broadband), clank (noise burst plus a ringing partial, for metal), sweep (a glide, for stings). `loop` clips are built to be seamless — a whole number of cycles at the given frequency.

motor.note: Low and dull. Pitched by road speed at runtime (T-6.18).

spin.note: The blade. Pitch tracks actual rpm, so spin-up is audible before it is dangerous.

detach.note: Deliberately the longest and loudest one-shot. Losing a part is the biggest thing that happens in a match and it should be the biggest thing you hear.

swing.note: The whoosh of a weapon that MISSES. battlebots.weaponSwing was the only event in the game with no listener at all, so an axe or flipper committing was silent (AUDIO-GAPS #1).

hammerHit.note: A swing weapon connecting. Distinct from `impact` so you can hear WHAT hit you, not just that something did.

impactHeavy.note: The top of the force curve. `impact` covers ordinary contact; this is for hits near shakeMaxForceN.

partBreak.note: A part reaching `destroyed`. VfxDirector already smokes a damaged part and fires a dead motor; this is the audio half (AUDIO-GAPS #2).

$tuningNote: T-6.18 / T-6.19. The pitch ranges are what make a motor sound like it is working rather than idling; the crowd figures are what make the room react to the fight instead of droning through it.
$fileNote: SOURCED AUDIO (2026-08-25). Every clip still has a full synthesis spec and is synthesised at load, exactly as before. A clip with a `file` ALSO fetches that mp3 and swaps the sampled version in once it decodes. Synthesis is therefore the floor, not the placeholder: a missing file, a 404, a decode failure or a browser that refuses the format all degrade to a sound that works rather than to silence, and the game is audible on the first frame instead of after a network round trip. Files live in `Audio/` in the repo and are copied to `<build>/audio/` by tools/rebuild-game.mjs; `fileBase` is where the running game looks for them.
